title: Godot 4.4.1 Stable and latest 4.5 already feel laggier compared to 4.4 Stable.
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in godot 4.4.1 Stable and 4.5 Dev 1 (although 4.5 is experimental so I understand that this should be treated as such)

The 4.4 release has excellent performance compared to these new releases.


### System information

Windows 10 - Godot 4.4.1 Stable - Godot 4.5 Dev1 and Dev2 - Nvidia GT 1030

### Issue description

I don't know why but Godot 4.4.1 Stable just feels laggier and more unstable compared to Godot 4.4. Godot 4.4 was excellent and much smoother than 4.3, but it's successors are going in a dangerous direction when it comes to performance in my opinion. This can likely be only noticed on weaker hardware as with everything, but it is very noticeable. Even affects the way player moves. There seems to be some sort of input lag or slower computing because in version 4.4 we have way more control over our player and it's very responsive. In newest version the player feels limited and seems to respond to input slower. Mostly visible when the movement applies friction, acceleration and deceleration.

The reason I think this issue will carry on potentially, is because 4.4.1 Stable came out and it is anything but stable from my experience. Game lags more in debug, and sometimes it's unplayable as if my game was incredibly complex. Then when I close and debug again, it is smoother and playable. This is concerning to me. Somewhere some drastic changes occured obviously in the new releases, and it affects the overall performance of new Godot version and I think the quicker it's identified the better.

### Steps to reproduce

Write any player movement logic which involves friction and acceleration/deceleration mechanics. Compare 4.4 Stable to both 4.4.1 Stable and 4.5 Dev 1 & 2 and see the clear difference in responsiveness yourself. And use the new TileMapLayer to create a small map with collisions.

Here's an example for player movement logic:

```gdscript
func _apply_movement(delta: float) -> void:
	var current_speed: float = weapon_speeds.get(speed_type, max_speed)
	var friction: float = current_speed * 0.65
	
	if movement_direction != Vector2.ZERO:
		current_velocity.x = move_toward(current_velocity.x, current_speed * movement_direction.x, 35 * delta * 60)
		current_velocity.y = move_toward(current_velocity.y, current_speed * movement_direction.y, 35 * delta * 60)
	else:
		current_velocity.x = move_toward(current_velocity.x, 0, friction * delta * 60)
		current_velocity.y = move_toward(current_velocity.y, 0, friction * delta * 60)
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The steps to reproduce are really easy, you should be able to spot the difference in any project that has any movement logic for player and loads a map with the new TileMapLayer. Here's some basic movement logic:

```gdscript
func _apply_movement(delta: float) -> void:
	var current_speed: float = weapon_speeds.get(speed_type, max_speed)
	var friction: float = current_speed * 0.65
	
	if movement_direction != Vector2.ZERO:
		current_velocity.x = move_toward(current_velocity.x, current_speed * movement_direction.x, 35 * delta * 60)
		current_velocity.y = move_toward(current_velocity.y, current_speed * movement_direction.y, 35 * delta * 60)
	else:
		current_velocity.x = move_toward(current_velocity.x, 0, friction * delta * 60)
		current_velocity.y = move_toward(current_velocity.y, 0, friction * delta * 60)
```
